metadata.title: Manipur- Life in relief camps | मणिपुर: रिलीफ़ कैंप में ज़िंदगी की जंग
metadata.description:
The conflict in Manipur has deep-rooted causes, primarily driven by ethnic faultlines and historical grievances among various communities in the region. Manipur, a northeastern state in India, is home to diverse ethnic groups, each with its own cultural, social, and economic aspirations. These ethnic tensions have led to sporadic outbreaks of violence and armed conflict over the years.

The displacement of over 60,000 people from their homes is a result of the ongoing conflict, which has forced them to seek refuge in relief camps. These camps provide basic humanitarian assistance and protection to the displaced population, but life in such camps is challenging, with limited access to resources and restricted movement due to daily curfews.
